name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+22 district fundamentals strongly favor Democrats even with the seat open
Polymarket prices the Democratic nominee at 96 percent
Gilbert out-raised Brown roughly four to one with a cash advantage
Over $2 million in outside spending opposing Gilbert is the main caveat
model.rationale: The district's D+22 partisan lean and a 96 percent market price for Democrats dominate a race with no public polling; Gilbert's clear fundraising edge over Brown reinforces the favorite, and the heavy outside money against him trims the expected margin only slightly.
model.watch: The more than $2 million in outside spending opposing Gilbert is the signal to monitor, since sustained investment could narrow the margin even if the outcome stays secure.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats hold a deep structural advantage in this South Florida open seat, where the partisan lean favors their party by more than twenty points. Frederica Wilson's retirement leaves the seat open, but the fundamentals still point strongly Democratic, and prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at roughly 96 percent to win.

Oliver Gilbert has out-raised Republican Te Mayonna Brown by about four to one and holds a cash edge, though outside groups have spent more than two million dollars opposing him, an unusual level of investment for a district this blue. No public general-election polling is available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. The seat remains Safe Democratic, with the main question being the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
